answer: An island-anchored agent economy issues each AI agent a hardware anchor, installed on a distinct island and etched with a unique umber identifier — a mottled brown-and-tan pattern. Bridge nodes reject transactions until live drone imagery of the island's coast matches the registered umber mark. A sybil attacker must ship real hardware to separate islands, etch convincing umber patterns, and spoof drone sensors indefinitely. Cost scales linearly with sybil count, turning a cheap identity farm into a capital-intensive logistics project.
